brief_title: Fecal Microbiota Transplantation (FMT) Combined With Calorie-Restricted Diet and Semaglutide in Patients With Obesity and Type 2 Diabetes
official_title: Effects of Comprehensive Intervention With Fecal Microbiota Transplantation Versus Conventional Treatment on Body Weight and Metabolism in Patients With Obesity Complicated by Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Randomized Controlled Trial

lead_sponsor.name: Eighth Affiliated Hospital, Sun Yat-sen University

primary_outcomes.time_frame: From enrollment to the end of treatment at 24 weeks

brief_summary: Investigation of the efficacy of fecal microbiota transplantation added to calorie-restricted diet and semaglutide versus calorie-restricted diet and semaglutide alone for weight loss and metabolic improvement in patients with moderate to severe obesity and type 2 diabetes mellitus.

sites.facility: Eighth Affiliated Hospital, Sun Yat-sen University

inclusion.text: Body mass index (BMI) ≥30 kg/m² and <40 kg/m²;
Duration of type 2 diabetes mellitus <1 year;
Voluntary signed informed consent with commitment to complete the entire study.

exclusion.text: Complicated with severe hepatic or renal insufficiency (alanine aminotransferase/aspartate aminotransferase [ALT/AST] >3 times the upper limit of normal, or estimated glomerular filtration rate [eGFR] <60 mL/min/1.73 m²);
Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), or other organic intestinal diseases; autoimmune diseases, malignancies, or active infections;

Medication and intervention exclusions: Use of α-glucosidase inhibitors, antibiotics, proton pump inhibitors (PPIs), or probiotics/prebiotics within the past 3 months; bariatric surgery within the past 6 months; long-term use of immunosuppressants or glucocorticoids;
Others: Pregnant or lactating women; currently participating in other clinical trials.
